title: Precursor Ratio-Controlled Chloride Vacancies in Lead-Free KCuCl3-x Memristors for Forming-Free Gradual Resistive Switching and Neuromorphic Learning
authors: Chinmayee Mandar Mhaskar, Sangeeta Roy Chaudhuri, Ayan Roy Chaudhuri
abstract: Defect engineering of memristive materials offers a powerful strategy for regulating ionic transport and analog resistive switching required for neuromorphic computing. Here, we report a wet chemical synthesis route for chloride-vacancy (VCl) engineering in lead-free all-inorganic KCuCl3-x thin films and establish a direct correlation between defect concentration, electronic structure, transport dynamics, and neuromorphic performance. Controlled precursor-ratio variation systematically tunes the VCl concentration in KCuCl3-x thin films, driving preferential vacancy formation at the terminal chloride sites, band-gap narrowing, and enhanced electronic disorder. W/KCuCl3-x/FTO memristors exhibit stable bipolar VCM-type resistive switching, with increasing VCl concentration promoting forming-free operation. An optimal VCl concentration (~ 1.3*10^21 cm^-3) provides a balance between ionic mobility and defect controllability, resulting in highly linear potentiation/depression characteristics and superior pulse endurance (>104 cycles). When the experimentally measured conductance characteristics of the optimized memristor are implemented as synaptic weights in artificial neural network simulations, recognition accuracies of 98.96% and 91.82% are achieved on the MNIST and Fashion-MNIST datasets, respectively. These findings establish precursor ratio-controlled VCl engineering as an effective strategy for simultaneously optimizing ionic transport, analog switching, and neuromorphic learning in lead-free halide perovskite memristors, providing a general materials design principle for energy-efficient neuromorphic electronics.
summary: This work demonstrates that by precisely controlling chloride vacancy concentration in lead-free $	ext{KCuCl}_{3-x}$ memristors using precursor chemistry, researchers can engineer the material's electronic structure and ionic transport. This control leads to superior, forming-free resistive switching, which is successfully mapped onto high-performance artificial neural network simulations.
main_problem: The goal is to develop a systematic method to optimize ionic transport, analog resistive switching, and overall neuromorphic learning performance simultaneously in lead-free halide perovskite memristors.
main_result: Controlling the chloride vacancy concentration ($	ext{VCl}$) via precursor ratio engineering provides an optimal balance, leading to forming-free gradual switching and achieving high recognition accuracies (e.g., 98.96% on MNIST).
method: The study combines wet chemical synthesis (varying precursor ratios) with comprehensive characterization techniques (XPS, XRD, UV-Vis) and electrical testing, culminating in artificial neural network simulations.
model_or_system: The physical system is a lead-free, all-inorganic $	ext{KCuCl}_{3-x}$ thin film used as a memristor. The mechanism relies on vacancy-mediated resistive switching, where the concentration of chloride vacancies ($	ext{VCl}$) is tuned by controlling the $	ext{KCl}:	ext{CuCl}_2$ precursor ratio.
key_observables: Chloride vacancy concentration ($	ext{VCl}$), electronic band gap ($	ext{E}_{	ext{g}}$), electronic disorder (Urbach energy), bipolar switching characteristics, and ANN recognition accuracy (MNIST/Fashion-MNIST).
important_parameters: Optimal $	ext{VCl}$ concentration ($\sim 1.3 	imes 10^{21} 	ext{ cm}^{-3}$), precursor molar ratio ($	ext{KCl}:	ext{CuCl}_2$), and cycle count (endurance).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that precursor-ratio control offers a simple and effective means to precisely regulate the concentration of mobile ionic defects ($	ext{VCl}$) within the perovskite lattice.
figures_summary: Figures likely show XRD patterns confirming structural stability across samples, XPS spectra detailing changes in elemental occupancy and bonding environments, and electrical I-V curves demonstrating the tunable resistive switching behavior.
paper_structure: The paper follows a progression from structural characterization (XRD, lattice parameters) to defect quantification (XPS, $	ext{VCl}$ concentration) to electronic property tuning ($	ext{E}_{	ext{g}}$, disorder) and finally to device performance validation (resistive switching, ANN simulation).
why_interesting: While the focus is on solid-state electronics, the explicit link between controlled structural disorder (vacancies) and the emergent computational behavior (synaptic weight modulation) touches upon concepts relevant to disordered quantum systems and glassy dynamics.
